description:
FILED s449 (Fable, round-7 review of agent Q) from an own-probe misfire whose divergence survived the clean re-probe.  PRE-EXISTING on main c8a8311 -- nothing to do with the dup work; reproduces on a plain empty file.

REPRO (perl 5.40.3):
    local $/;
    open(my $fh, "<", $empty_file) or die;
    my $x = <$fh>;          # perl: defined, length 0     PCL: undef
    my $y = <$fh>;          # perl: undef                 PCL: undef
Line mode ($/ = "\n") answers undef on both sides -- the quirk is slurp-only.
Same shape through an fdopen of an exhausted descriptor: open(my $d, "<&=" . fileno($s)) after $s slurped -- perl def[0], PCL undef.

Perl rule: in slurp mode the FIRST readline returns everything from here to EOF, and "nothing" is the empty string, a defined value; only a repeat read answers undef.  Programs test defined() on a slurp to mean "the open handle was readable at all".

FIX SHAPE: %p-readline-impl (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp) slurp arm answers "" instead of nil the first time; needs a per-read decision, not per-handle state -- perl re-answers "" after a seek back to EOF (probe that before implementing).  BAR: the three-row repro above + the seek-back probe + a nonempty-file inverse vs perl; a Pl/t guard row; cl/ change so the io/ companion leg at the next sweep.

NOTE (s518d resume #2, 2026-10-18): perl's t/io/argv.t loses 2 rows to this (the in-place loop over tmpIo_argv1.tmp + the EMPTY tmpIo_argv2.tmp with $/ = undef never takes its second turn); baselines/row-shortfall.tsv t/io/argv.t cites it.  Probe: scratch/s518d/pr/slurp.pl and inpl.pl in the s518d worktree (perl got[2] got[0], PCL got[2] only).


=== DONE (s538a, Opus, 2026-11-12 .. 11-13; commits fa9586da cl/ + 8de505ed guard 21d + 65f55e45 ir-spec; branch hashes before the merge) ===
perl's rule is PER-HANDLE state, not per-read: IOf_NOLINE (pp_hot.c do_readline sets it beside IoLINES++ when a
readline ANSWERS a record; only an open clears it -- doio.c openn_cleanup).  SNARF_EOF: a SCALAR-context slurp at EOF on
a handle with NOLINE clear answers "" (and counts it, $. 1).  Probed 5.40.3: the seek-back probe answers UNDEF (seek does
not reset it); a handle that answered a line answers undef; read/getc/eof beside it change nothing; list context on an
empty file is (); a dup / fdopen / reopen / each <> file is fresh; in-memory and pipe handles alike; a directory read
(failure) stays undef.  Encoded in the existing $. table *p-fh-lines* (a FIXNUM once answered, (COUNT) before; `$. = N`
and the <> seed keep a handle fresh) -- one CONSP test per line, no second EOF table (the *p-eof-seen* EOF flag is a
different fact: seek clears it, not NOLINE).  Probes scratch/s538a/pr/s660a.pl + s660b.pl: 54 lines, tree = perl, base
wrong on 26; the s539 review's PIPE shapes (pr2/pipes.pl, 17 lines) and the locked-append shape (pr2/lockapp.pl): tree =
perl, base wrong on 5.  Guards Pl/t/fileio-02.t 21c + 21d (pipes + locked append), both fail on the base.
BOARD: Path-Tiny input_output.t / _no_PU_UU.t / _no_UU.t (perl 57 each): base 2 ok then died rc 255 -> the files now run
past the slurp and HANG (TIMEOUT at 120 s, *FILE* no TAP rows rc=124) on a lock held by a RETURNED handle -- POINT 4,
#2006 PART 2 (noted there with the reproducer; NS:ns-escaping-filehandle), NOT a regression of this fix: the base hangs on
the same plain-Perl reduction.  With PERL_PATH_TINY_NO_FLOCK=1 each runs to its plan, 45 ok / 12 not ok (rows 40-51 =
the same escaping handle, unflushed).  Rows re-keyed BY EDIT (*PLAN* #660 -> *FILE* NS:ns-escaping-filehandle).
CLOSE-WITH-ROWS: the three *PLAN* rows keyed #660 left the board baseline (re-keyed); no board row is keyed #660 now.
